subject: Budget range validation: monthly spend & procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@enterprise-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Budget range validation: monthly spend & procurement thresholds

Hi Alex — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put a formal quote together: 

1) Recap of what I heard on the call:
- Primary use: customer support and automated reconciliation flows (high-throughput generation + embedding lookups).
- Expected baseline: ~500M tokens/month (inbound+generated).
- Peak: up to ~1B tokens in high months.
- Typical request size: 1.5k–3k tokens.

2) Pricing / budget items we need you to validate:
- Do those baseline/peak token numbers look right? If you can give a conservative monthly range (min — typical — max) that helps a lot.
- Do you have a target unit economics target ($/1M tokens) or an internal budget band we should aim for (e.g., $X–$Y per month)?
- Procurement/PO thresholds: at what monthly/annual spend do you need a PO/contract/SOW? Any internal approval gates we should know about?

3) Next steps from our side:
- I’ll loop in our pricing lead (Marissa) for an initial tiered quote + a committed-reserved option that lowers the $/1M at higher commitments.
- If you can share procurement thresholds and a preferred decision timeline, we’ll tailor the contract and SOW accordingly.

Thanks — I’ll wait to confirm the numbers and then Marissa will send the pricing sheet.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@enterprise-payments.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@enterprise-payments.com
Date: 2026-06-15T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation: monthly spend & procurement thresholds

Thanks for the follow-up and the clear recap, Rishi. Confirming details from our side: 

- Token volumes: baseline ~400–600M tokens/month (safety buffer assume 600M). Peak months could push to ~1B tokens depending on campaign volume.
- Budget band: our finance team gave a preliminary target of $5k–$25k/month for this initial phase (we're flexible if committed discounts change the unit economics).
- Unit economics target: the product team is aiming for effective cost ~ $8–$12 per 1M tokens (this is internal target to be profitable on our integration). 
- Procurement thresholds: any vendor spend above $5,000/month requires procurement notification and a simple vendor assessment. Any multi-year or >$200k/year commitment will require formal legal review and a signed master services agreement + SOW.
- Decision timeline: pilot decision within 4–6 weeks, production contract within 2–3 months if pilot meets SLA/cost expectations.

A couple of clarifying Qs: do you have a standard committed tier that covers ~600M/month? Also, do you support invoice/PO billing?

Appreciate the quick turn — looping procurement for visibility.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering
Enterprise Payments
alex.j@enterprise-payments.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-15T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Budget range validation: monthly spend & procurement thresholds

Marissa / Dylan — forwarding Alex's note. Key asks: baseline 400–600M (use 600M as conservative), peak ~1B; customer target $8–$12 per 1M tokens and procurement triggers at $5k/month and >$200k/year for legal. They asked whether we have a committed tier around ~600M/month and if we support invoice/PO billing. Can you draft a tiered pricing + committed discount option and confirm billing / PO flow?

I suggested we provide: 
- Pay-as-you-go price (no commit) for quick pilot
- 6–12 month committed tier at discounted $/1M with a monthly committed volume and overage pricing
- Reserved/dedicated options with SLA + pricing for >1B/month scale

Please attach the pricing PDF and a short note we can send to procurement. Alex is aiming to make a pilot decision in 4–6 weeks.

Thanks,
Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@enterprise-payments.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@enterprise-payments.com
Date: 2026-06-15T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation: monthly spend & procurement thresholds — pricing sheet attached

Hi Alex — thanks for the details. Attaching our suggested pricing tiers and a short procurement note to simplify your vendor assessment. Short summary below: 

Suggested pricing (examples based on token volumes):
- Pay-as-you-go (no commitment): $12 per 1M tokens
- Committed (6–12 month) tiers:
  • 0.5B/month committed: $9 per 1M tokens (monthly commit 500M, overage billed at $11/1M)
  • 1B/month committed: $7 per 1M tokens (monthly commit 1B, overage billed at $9/1M)
- Reserved/Dedicated (SLA-backed): pricing and discounts available for multi-region reserved capacity; requires a conversation with our infra team for exact sizing and a minimum contract (typically starts at $20k/month).

Billing & procurement:
- We support invoiced/PO billing for enterprise customers. Procurement threshold notes: purchases > $5k/month will generate a vendor questionnaire; > $200k/year triggers legal MSA review.

Attachments included:
- redwood-pricing-tiers-20260615.pdf (pricing grid + illustrative math)
- SOW-template.docx (standard SOW to speed procurement)

If the $9/1M tier at 0.5B/month looks reasonable, we can draft a pilot agreement with a 3-month commit to give you guaranteed pricing and predictable spend for procurement. Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement/legal to walk through the attachment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Pricing & GTM — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-pricing-tiers-20260615.pdf (application/pdf); SOW-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
